Energy-efficient windows meet standards like Government’s ENERGY STAR® certification and feature ratings such as U-factor and Low-E glass, which help reduce heat transfer and improve comfort. Why do I get condensation on my windows? Condensation usually occurs when warm indoor air meets cold glass. While occasional condensation is normal, persistent moisture between panes may indicate a failed seal. Will new windows reduce drafts and outside noise? Yes, modern windows with advanced sealing and insulated glass can significantly reduce drafts and outside noise, improving indoor comfort. What window materials are best for energy efficiency? Vinyl, fiberglass, and wood-clad windows all offer strong energy performance when properly manufactured and installed. The best choice depends on durability, maintenance preferences, and design goals. Will new windows or doors save me money on energy bills? Upgrading to energy-efficient windows and doors with Peach can help reduce heat loss, air leakage, and drafts, which lowers your heating and cooling costs. Plus, many local utility programs offer rebates for energy-efficient products, making your investment even more affordable. Actual savings will depend on your home, climate, and the efficiency of the products installed. What makes a window energy efficient? Energy-efficient windows use a combination of features: double or triple-pane glass filled with insulating argon gas, Low-E (low-emissivity) coatings that reflect UV and infrared heat, thermally broken frames that prevent conduction, and precision-fit weatherstripping that eliminates drafts. Together, these features are measured by U-factor (heat transfer rate) and Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC). Government ENERGY STAR-certified windows meet or exceed federal efficiency standards for your climate zone. What is a U-factor, and what should I look for in Utah? U-factor measures how well a window resists heat loss — lower is better. For Northern Utah, ENERGY STAR recommends 0.27 or lower. Peach Building Products can help you pick windows that meet your needs and qualify for local energy rebates. Can I get a tax credit for replacing my windows with energy-efficient ones? Yes. Under the federal Inflation Reduction Act, homeowners may qualify for an Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit of up to 30% of the cost of qualifying ENERGY STAR-certified windows (up to $600 per year for windows). Consult your tax advisor to confirm eligibility, and ask Peach Building Products which products qualify when requesting your quote. Are your windows costing you money every month? Possibly, yes. Especially if single-glass pane windows or old double-pane units with failed seals allow significant heat transfer — up to 30% of your home’s total energy loss. Upgrading to modern energy-efficient replacement windows reduces that loss dramatically, lowering your heating and cooling costs year-round. Contact Us How should I prepare my home for installation day? Clear access to the windows and doors that will be worked on, and remove any nearby furniture, wall décor, or other obstacles. Make sure to remove blinds, shades, or other items that may be in the way to give the installers full access. Secure pets and ensure the work area is safe. Your installer will provide specific preparation instructions tailored to your home and project. Do I need permits to replace windows or doors? Permits may be required, especially if structural changes are involved. A professional contractor typically handles permitting when necessary. Do contractors remove and dispose of old windows and doors? Most professional installers include removal and disposal as part of the project, but it’s always best to confirm this in advance. How long does window or door installation take? Most window or door installations take a few hours per unit. Full-home replacements typically take one to several days, depending on the scope of work, home conditions, size of replacement windows and number. Can I install windows or doors myself? While DIY installation is possible, professional installation is recommended to ensure proper sealing, performance, and warranty coverage. Improper installation can lead to drafts, leaks, and structural issues. How do I prepare my home for window installation day? Before your installation crew arrives: clear furniture and window treatments from the immediate area of each window being replaced (about 3 feet of clearance), remove any fragile items from nearby shelves or walls (vibration during removal can shake things loose), ensure pets are secured away from the work area, and make sure your installer has clear access to each window inside and outside. Our team handles the rest. What warranty covers the installation work itself?
